extension.name: xcomm
extension.description: Reviews xcomm control-socket commands that act on a real serial device: text and bytes sent to the board (ctl send, ctl run), line control (break, DTR/RTS, line settings), zmodem/ymodem/xmodem transfers, and captures written to local files. Commands that only observe (ctl status, read, wait, sessions) are left unmatched. Opening a session directly (xcomm <device>, which also sends piped stdin and raises DTR/RTS) is outside this extension. Boundary reviewed against xcomm 0.1.3.
safer_alternatives: Use xcomm ctl <device> read --since <offset> or wait to observe the board without sending anything.
Start the session with --ctl ro so the control socket allows status and reads only.

permissions.label: Send input to a serial device
permissions.description: Sends text or raw bytes to the board on the session's serial port. Whatever is listening there runs it: a shell, a bootloader such as U-Boot, or firmware. A send cannot be taken back, and a reply prompt is not proof the command ran.
safer_guidance: Read the session's output first (xcomm ctl <device> read --last 4096) to see which prompt the board is at.
Give run a --fail-on pattern for boot banners or error text so a reboot is not taken as success.

permissions.label: Control serial line signals and settings
permissions.description: Sends a break, sets or pulses DTR/RTS, or changes baud, data bits, parity, stop bits or flow control. On many boards DTR/RTS are wired to reset or boot-mode pins, and a break can stop a bootloader or trigger a console SysRq.
safer_guidance: Check the board's wiring before toggling DTR/RTS; on auto-reset boards a pulse resets the target.

permissions.label: Transfer files over the serial line
permissions.description: Runs lrzsz on the session's port: send pushes local files to the device; recv writes files from the device. zmodem and ymodem recv write only below the working directory; xmodem recv writes to the path given, wherever it is.
safer_guidance: Check the file list and the receiving program on the board before a send; run zmodem or ymodem recv in a scratch directory, and check the target path of an xmodem recv.
permissions.example_command: xcomm ctl ttyUSB1 xfer send zmodem firmware.bin

permissions.label: Write a capture file
permissions.description: Starts or stops appending the device's output to a local file chosen by the caller.
safer_guidance: Capture into a new file in a scratch directory; the session appends to an existing file.
permissions.example_command: xcomm ctl ttyUSB1 capture start boot.log

rules.title: xcomm serial device input
rules.description: Identifies xcomm ctl send and ctl run, which put text, --hex bytes or a --file's bytes on the serial line. Matches the subcommand word anywhere in an xcomm ctl invocation before `--`, because the device name (or --pane) comes between ctl and the subcommand and the word can follow options. Two limits follow. A subcommand after `--` (xcomm ctl -- ttyUSB1 send ls) is not seen, so it keeps only the unknown-executable review floor and a disabled permission does not block it. A matching word elsewhere in the line counts as the subcommand: option text or a wait pattern (--fail-on set, wait run), the text of a send or run (send set), or xfer's direction (xfer send also hits device input). A disabled permission then also blocks that command; this fails closed. dtr, rts, xfer and capture also need the word xcomm requires after them (on/off/toggle/pulse, send/recv, start/stop), so a status field such as status capture does not match. No help-flag exemption is granted: xcomm takes the word after a value option as its value, so --help can be a --until pattern while the send still happens. xcomm ctl status, read, wait and sessions only observe the session and are outside these rules.
safer_alternatives: Use xcomm ctl <device> wait or read to observe the board without sending.

rules.title: xcomm serial line control
rules.description: Identifies xcomm ctl break, dtr, rts and set. Matches the subcommand word anywhere in an xcomm ctl invocation before `--`, because the device name (or --pane) comes between ctl and the subcommand and the word can follow options. Two limits follow. A subcommand after `--` (xcomm ctl -- ttyUSB1 send ls) is not seen, so it keeps only the unknown-executable review floor and a disabled permission does not block it. A matching word elsewhere in the line counts as the subcommand: option text or a wait pattern (--fail-on set, wait run), the text of a send or run (send set), or xfer's direction (xfer send also hits device input). A disabled permission then also blocks that command; this fails closed. dtr, rts, xfer and capture also need the word xcomm requires after them (on/off/toggle/pulse, send/recv, start/stop), so a status field such as status capture does not match.
safer_alternatives: Use xcomm ctl <device> status to read the line settings and modem lines without changing them.

rules.title: xcomm serial file transfer
rules.description: Identifies xcomm ctl xfer send and recv with zmodem, ymodem or xmodem. Matches the subcommand word anywhere in an xcomm ctl invocation before `--`, because the device name (or --pane) comes between ctl and the subcommand and the word can follow options. safer_alternatives: Review the files and the board's receiving program before transferring.

rules.title: xcomm local capture write
rules.description: Identifies xcomm ctl capture start and stop, which append device output to a caller-chosen local file. Matches the subcommand word anywhere in an xcomm ctl invocation before `--`, because the device name (or --pane) comes between ctl and the subcommand and the word can follow options. Two limits follow. A subcommand after `--` (xcomm ctl -- ttyUSB1 send ls) is not seen, so it keeps only the unknown-executable review floor and a disabled permission does not block it. A matching word elsewhere in the line counts as the subcommand: option text or a wait pattern (--fail-on set, wait run), the text of a send or run (send set), or xfer's direction (xfer send also hits device input). A disabled permission then also blocks that command; this fails closed. dtr, rts, xfer and capture also need the word xcomm requires after them (on/off/toggle/pulse, send/recv, start/stop), so a status field such as status capture does not match.
safer_alternatives: Use xcomm ctl <device> read --from-oldest to fetch the kept output without writing a file.
